facts.text: Middleborough was first settled by Europeans in 1661 and officially incorporated as a town in 1669 after changing its name from Nemasket to Middleborough.
The Oliver Estate, built in the 1700s by Judge Peter Oliver for his son and daughter‑in‑law, remains a cornerstone of Middleborough’s colonial heritage.
Every October, the historic Oliver Estate hosts a free Colonial Re‑Enactment that lets visitors experience 18th‑century life with drills, musket demos, and hands‑on crafts.
Two freight rail lines cross Middleborough: CSX Transportation runs the Boston and Taunton line, while Massachusetts Coastal Railroad serves the Cape Cod and Taunton line.
The town hall at 10 Nickerson Avenue is reputedly one of Middleborough’s most haunted buildings, a legend that dates back to the 19th century.
Middleborough’s public library, located downtown, is part of a network that traces its roots to the nation’s first circulating public library system founded by Enoch Pratt.
